title: WPMS/2152/2018 of Naval Hydrographic Office Workers Union Vs Chairman Upsc Dholpur House Shahjahan Road AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2152 of 2018
Naval Hydrographic Office Workers Union
 ..........Petitioner
 Versus
Chairman UPSC, Dholpur House & others

...Respondents
Present:- Mr. Tarun Lakhera, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. N.S. Pundir, Advocate for respondent no. 1.
 Mr. Shivanand Bhatt, Central Government Standing Counsel for the
 Union of India/respondent nos. 2 to 4.
 Mr. K.H. Gupta, Advocate for the intervener.

Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
 The petitioner before this Court is a registered
Union of Naval Hydrographic Office Workers (Civilians). They
have filed the present writ petition challenging the selection
process for the post of Civil Hydrographic Officer for the
Institute known as Naval Hydrographic Office, Dehradun.
2. The main contention of the petitioner before this
Court is that the certificate of an Institute, namely, the
Institution of Surveyors, which is based in Delhi is being taken
into consideration, whereas the fact is that the certificate of
this Institute stands derecognized by the All India Council for
Technical Education (in short "AICTE").
3. The selection process was stayed by this Court
vide its order dated 11.09.2018.
4. Meanwhile, counter affidavit and rejoinder
affidavit have been exchanged between the parties.

2
5. In this case, an intervention application has also
been filed by the selected candidate, who inter alia, has also
challenged the locus standi of the present petitioner for filing
the present writ petition. It is alleged that the petitioner was
not a candidate in the selection process but it is merely a
Union of Civil Workers of Naval establishment.
6. Admittedly it is not a case where the selected
candidate is aggrieved by the selection process or even by any
order of the respondents. There is technically no locus standi
of the petitioner.
7. All the same, this Court in the larger interest
would not dismiss the petition as the issue raised here is
important.
8. It has also been brought in the counter affidavit
filed by the intervener that the intervener in any case is a
qualified person and the certificate which he has from the
Institution of Surveyors although is a valid certificate, but was
only an additional qualification he has, meaning that even if
this certificate, regarding which a dispute has been raised
here, is not taken into consideration, he still has the requisite
qualifications.
9. As per the Recruitment Rules, the post of Civil
Hydrographic Officer has the following essential
qualifications:-
 "(i) Degree in Engineering or
Masters degree in Mathematics or
Geography or Geophysics
OR
(i) Pass in the final examination
of the institution of surveyors
in sub-division 1 (b)
Hydrographic surveying.

3
(ii) 2 years experience as a
qualified Surveying officer in a
recognised Hydrographic
Service."
10. The essential qualification is either a candidate
should have a Degree in Engineering or Master Degree in
Mathematics or Geography or Geophysics or he should have
passed in the final examination of the institution of surveyors
in sub-division 1 or 2 years experience as a qualified
Surveying officer in a recognised Hydrographic Service.
11. The desirable qualifications for the post of Civil
Hydrographic Officer are as follows:-
 "(i) Knowledge of a foreign
language, preferably French.
 (ii) Knowledge of Computer
operations and Geographical
Information System.
 Note 1.- qualifications are
relaxable at the discretion of Union
Public Service Commission in or
case of candidates otherwise well
qualified.
 Note 2.- The qualification(s)
regarding experience is/are
relaxable at the discretion of the
Union Public Service Commission in
case of candidates belonging to
Scheduled Caste or Scheduled
Tribes. If at any stage of selection
the Union Public Service
Commission is of the opinion that
sufficient number of candidates
from these communities possessing
the requisite experience are not
likely to be available to fill up the
posts reserved for them."
12. Admittedly, the intervener has a minimum
qualification as he has done his Masters in Geography. The
two years of experience certificate has been given to him by
the National Hydrographic Office of India. This certificate

4
though is of a period when the said Institute was still
recognized. The de-recognition of the Institute is by an office
memorandum of the Government of India dated 10.07.2012,
by which it has derecognized the Institution of Surveyor.
However, the office memorandum dated 10.07.2012 was
withdrawn by the Government of India vide order dated
06.12.2012 and the clarification which was given is as
follows:-
 "In modification of Order F.No.11-
15/2011-AR (TS.II) dated 10.07.2012 and to
facilitate the institutions during transition period,
following decision has been taken in the Ministry:
(i) Above order dated 10.07.2012 regarding
cases of recognition in perpetuity for
equivalence in Central Government job,
stands withdrawn.
(ii) All those students who are enrolled with the
institutions with permanent recognition
upto 31.05.2013 would be eligible for
consideration in accordance with MHRD
office memorandum/order in force
pertaining to their course for equivalence in
Central Government jobs. However, these
concerned orders will cease to have effect
from 01.06.2013 onwards.
(iii) After 31.05.2013, based on the review by
the regulator i.e. AICTE, a decision on
continuation of the certification of
equivalence of degree/diploma shall be
taken by statutory regulator.
(iv) Statutory regulators should review the fresh
proposals/extension as per their statute
and regulations.
2. In case, the institution desires to opt for
realigning curriculum with NVEQF, it is advised
to use this transition period upto 30.05.2013 for
necessary action in this regard.
 This issues with the approval of the
Competent Authority."

13. Therefore, the institute stood derecognized from
31.05.2013. Further the office memorandum dated
06.12.2012 shows that the Institute has been derecognized
after 01.06.2013. However, any person who has procured a

5
certificate from the Institute prior to 01.06.2013, the said
certificate will be considered to be a valid certificate.
14. Admittedly, the private respondent/intervener
has got his certificate prior to the said date. Therefore, his
certificate cannot be said to be invalid in law. Although since
the certificate of the Institution of Surveyors stands
derecognized after 01.06.2013, such a certificate cannot be
considered as an essential qualification. All the same, the
intervener has in any case, a minimum qualification of Master
Degree in Geography and therefore he has the minimum
qualification, even if his certificate is not considered.
15. In view thereof, the writ petition stands
dismissed. A direction is hereby issued to the concerned
authority to take a decision in the matter in accordance with
law as expeditiously as possible.
16. Interim order dated 11.09.2018 is hereby
vacated.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 31.10.2019
Ankit/
